lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice present perfect for simple experiences.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Colleagues chat about places, food, and small life experiences.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Asking whether someone has done or tried something.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik talk at fika about whether they have been to Malmö, tried a Swedish snack, or met a colleague before.

main_focus.name: present perfect for experiences
main_focus.description: Use har plus supine to ask about or state simple life experiences without focusing on a specific past time.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use present perfect naturally 4-6 times in the dialogue.

allowed_supporting_grammar: main-clause negation with aldrig or inte
preterite only for one brief follow-up if needed
avoid_grammar: detailed contrast between preterite and present perfect

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use experience phrases that naturally arise in getting-to-know-you conversation.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker asks whether the other has tried or visited something familiar.
dialogue_shape.middle: They exchange a few present-perfect experiences with short reactions.
dialogue_shape.ending: They mention one thing they may try or visit later, without shifting into a future-focused lesson.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat har plus supine in questions and statements

focus: which experience one speaker has had
which experience one speaker has never had
what food or place is mentioned

sentence_focus: one question with har du varit
one negative experience sentence with aldrig
one short reaction to an experience
